goal: Make a thawed guest report a VM Generation ID change, and prove it with a disposable thaw on 45.76.77.97 before the fleet boot kernel is replaced. Mjolnir.Thaw.Vmgenid.observe/1 currently returns :missing. Add a guest-agent report of the generation id the VMGENID driver exposes, and thread that report through observe/1 so Mjolnir.Thaw.Vmgenid.verify/2 can see a real id. A /dev/urandom sample after Entropy.reseed is not that report. Entropy.reseed still finishes before the guest is reachable over vsock, and before PTY, ticket, and gateway publish. On root@45.76.77.97, record that the cloud-hypervisor binary is a v54+ build containing VmGenId. Build the x86_64 PVH kernel with scripts/build-kernel.sh (CONFIG_VMGENID=y is already in that script). Cold-boot one disposable VM on that kernel, freeze it, and thaw it. The guest must observe a generation id different from the id stored at capture. Do not copy the new kernel over /var/lib/mjolnir/vmlinux-ch until that observation exists. A second thaw of that same snapshot, while the first guest is still running, gets a new VM id, vsock CID, virtiofsd socket, and TAP, over a clone of the pinned rootfs, and no gateway ticket. The two guests must observe different generation ids. The first guest stays published if the second thaw fails. Check the open boxes in openspec/changes/add-vmgenid/tasks.md only for proofs you actually ran. Leave the change banner ACTIVE BUILD.
non_goals: A new guest IP, MAC, or Iroh key for the second thaw

anchors.invariant: Returns a guest-visible generation id, never a urandom sample taken after Entropy.reseed. :missing means the guest did not report the device id.
A CONFIG_VMGENID capture with a missing or unchanged id is not published. A legacy record does not claim a generation-id change.
Still gates vsock reachability, PTY, ticket, and gateway. It is not evidence the VMGENID driver ran.

acceptance.journey: On 45.76.77.97, a disposable VM cold-booted on a CONFIG_VMGENID=y kernel is frozen and thawed. The guest observes a generation id different from the id recorded at capture. That observation is not a /dev/urandom read after Entropy.reseed. The fleet file /var/lib/mjolnir/vmlinux-ch is unchanged until that observation exists. A second thaw of the same snapshot, while the first guest is running, is vsock-reachable after reseed, has no gateway ticket, and observes a different generation id. The first guest is still published if that second thaw fails. mix test test/mjolnir/vmgenid_thaw_test.exs passes.

replace /var/lib/mjolnir/vmlinux-ch before a disposable thaw shows a new generation id
give the second guest a gateway ticket or a new IP, MAC, or Iroh key
